+---
+name: asdg-decision
+description: Analyze, compare, document, or revisit a material ASDG decision using the current project and specialist context. Use for architectural trade-offs as well as product choices; preserves Focus and operational authority.
+---
+
+# ASDG Decision
+
+Use this conversation's decision, purpose, constraints, evidence, and human choices; do not restart a completed discussion.
+Recognize `$asdg-decision` and “asdg decision” as this conversational skill, not a new CLI subcommand.
+Resolve the client from this canonical directory as `../../..`; read its instructions, [session policy](../asdg-focus/session-policy.md), and fresh local CLI status.
+Use current verified context when available. Ask only for missing information that would materially change the analysis or destination.
+
+## Resolve context and intent
+
+Identify the decision subject, affected project, selected specialist (including None or Unknown), and requested action.
+A selected role defines the perspective; an explicit user assignment defines the subject. Neither reading this skill nor inferring an owner changes Focus.
+Distinguish methodology maintenance from a decision about the consuming application.
+For an architecture subject assigned to ASDG-05, read [foundational guidance](../../05-high-level-design-and-architecture/docs/architectural-decisions.md) and its [contract](../../05-high-level-design-and-architecture/types/contract.md).
+For another context, read the actual owner's contract; adapt criteria and destination to that responsibility. Do not send all decisions to Stage 05.
+Without a selected role, use the explicit task and evidence to identify a proposed owner without activating it. If ownership or destination matters and remains ambiguous, clarify it.
+A request for analysis only returns analysis. A request to record/document, or an existing assigned documentation task, saves within applicable authority; never ask again for already granted authorization.
+A bare invocation continues the evident task; if intent is unknown, analyze provisionally and clarify the missing action before writing.
+
+## Analyze and record
+
+Explain the desired outcome and why a choice matters before describing mechanisms.
+Compare the few viable options, including the current approach or no change when meaningful; compare equivalent responsibilities and separate complements.
+Consider relevant quality attributes, constraints, costs, failure modes, reversibility, migration effort, and evidence gaps; avoid arbitrary scoring.
+Distinguish verified behavior, vendor claims, inference, and untested expectations. Verify unstable external claims with primary sources.
+Carry forward an explicit human selection; otherwise label the choice proposed or undecided. A framework recommendation is not measured superiority.
+For documentation, follow [the decision package format](record-format.md); use [the worked example](example.md) as guidance, not a fixed product list.
+Reuse the existing decision package when revisiting it; preserve the previous choice, evidence, rationale, and reasons for change.
+Deliver a concise recommendation or record link, consequences, and the evidence that would justify revisiting the decision.
+
+## Boundaries
+
+The ASDG-05 contract permits bounded decision-document authoring for assigned architecture work; no application sprint is needed for those documents.
+Other contexts retain their own write limits. Discovery alone grants no writes, role activation, delegation, or state transitions.
+Selection records describe the human's stated choice; they do not approve newly written bytes or trigger implementation.
+Preserve lifecycle/sprint state and review history. Formal acceptance uses the existing approval workflow only when explicitly requested.
+Respect runtime denials; preserve the analysis and report the exact blocked write rather than bypassing controls.
+

+# A decision package readers can understand
+
+One material decision gets one named folder, one or two introductory documents, and short assessments of its meaningful alternatives.
+Use this format for boundaries, deployment, data ownership, interaction patterns, reliability, security, and build-versus-buy choices as well as products.
+
+![Explain the outcome, compare alternatives, record the choice and consequences, then define evidence for revisiting.](images/decision-record.svg)
+
+## Location and reading order
+
+Use the bound client's existing decision location within the responsible stage. ASDG-05 defaults to `docs/asdg/05-high-level-design-and-architecture/decisions/<Decision name>/`.
+Honor a supplied safe folder name; otherwise use a descriptive decision title. Search existing decisions first and avoid duplicates.
+For an undecided question, use a neutral title. A later choice can update the record without silently moving it or breaking links.
+This is a topic-folder exception to the shared flat stage layout; its numbered filenames express reading order, not Intended/Actual/Planned categories.
+
+| File | What the reader learns |
+| --- | --- |
+| `README.md` | Decision/question, status, scope, why it matters, choice or recommendation, consequences, and navigation. |
+| `01-comparison.md` when useful | Context, decision drivers, comparable options, evidence, uncertainties, and reasons for the choice. |
+| One short document per meaningful option | Responsibility, fit, trade-offs, why selected/deferred, and conditions for reconsideration. |
+| `images/` | Editable sources of diagrams embedded in the relevant documents. |
+
+Scale the package to the decision; combine introductory material when small and do not create filler options.
+Give each substantive explanation a useful visual of behavior, boundaries, relationships, failure paths, or evidence.
+A comparison/status table alone is not the explanatory visual. Navigation-only indexes retain the shared exception.
+Keep every Markdown unit within 50 nonblank source lines, with readable paragraphs and spacing.
+
+## Decision integrity and delivery
+
+Record proposed, selected, deferred, or superseded status in prose, identifying the actual basis and known date.
+State the selected scope/horizon and material consequences, including obligations and accepted trade-offs.
+Link evidence and related decisions; retain uncertainty and absent measurements. Do not fabricate consensus, scores, approvals, or implementation results.
+Capture concrete revisit triggers and the observation or experiment that could change the choice.
+When revising, retain the earlier decision and explain what evidence changed; preserve existing review history and registered artifact bytes unless the task calls for edits.
+Check local links, source length, and every new/changed diagram at realistic document width; inspect representative complete rendered pages.
+Record each document's visual, explanatory purpose, and actual inspection result with its hash-bound AI modification receipt under the [documentation standard](../../00-governance/docs/documentation-standard.md).
+Use the [review criteria](../../00-governance/docs/documentation-review.md); report specific unavailable checks. A document saved is not a human-approved baseline.
+

+# Explain why the architecture takes this shape
+
+ASDG-05 treats every material high-level architecture decision as an evidence-based choice with consequences.
+A choice is material when it affects system boundaries, quality attributes, dependencies, data/control ownership, deployment, or expensive future change.
+Routine implementation details do not become architectural decisions merely to populate documentation.
+
+![Desired outcome and constraints guide alternatives, the decision and its consequences, and evidence for revisiting.](../../skills/asdg-decision/images/decision-record.svg)
+
+## Foundational reasoning
+
+Start with the desired user or operational outcome and constraints; explain why a choice is needed before how it works.
+Identify the responsibility being assigned and compare viable ways to satisfy it, including the existing approach when relevant.
+Separate layers and complementary capabilities; a tool for evaluation is not necessarily a competitor to an execution runtime.
+Judge relevant latency, reliability, consistency, security, operability, cost, portability, and maintainability trade-offs in this project's context.
+State uncertainty and the limits of evidence. Provider ownership, popularity, a feature list, or a diagram does not establish fitness.
+Prefer the smallest sufficient commitment with explicit consequences and a practical path to change it.
+
+## Durable decision knowledge
+
+Document all material decisions produced by assigned architecture documentation work using [ASDG Decision](../../skills/asdg-decision/SKILL.md) and its [package format](../../skills/asdg-decision/record-format.md).
+Preserve the current discussion and explicit human selection; distinguish a recommendation from a selected direction.
+Cover patterns, placements, interfaces, ownership, resilience, and data choices as well as frameworks and products.
+Use short visual explanations: one named decision folder, one or two introductions, and one note per meaningful alternative.
+State why the choice is sufficient now, what it costs or constrains, and concrete conditions for revisiting it.
+Link a decision to relevant architecture documents within the assigned documentation scope; keep each decision discoverable through its comparison/index.
+The [worked example](../../skills/asdg-decision/example.md) illustrates the method without becoming a dependency on its client or vendor.
+
+## Assignment and authority
+
+An analysis-only question can remain conversational. Assigned documentation includes the material decisions it produces; do not repeatedly ask to save them.
+The [ASDG-05 contract](../types/contract.md) bounds decision writes and distinguishes them from application implementation and formal acceptance.
+A decision record is evidence of reasoning and stated selection, not proof of runtime behavior or authorization to execute the choice.
+

+# Context-aware decision analysis and documentation
+
+ASDG Decision turns a material choice into short visual explanations of its purpose, alternatives, consequences, and revisit conditions.
+The user requested this methodology change after reviewing SpeakerCoach's OpenAI Agents SDK decision package.
+The skill covers architecture patterns, boundaries, placement and ownership as well as product selection.
+
+![Why a choice matters leads to comparable alternatives, a bounded choice and concrete revisit evidence.](../../../asdg/skills/asdg-decision/images/decision-record.svg)
+
+## What changed
+
+[ASDG Decision](../../../asdg/skills/asdg-decision/SKILL.md) preserves the current project, specialist, discussion and explicit choices; analysis-only requests remain conversational.
+[ASDG-05 foundations](../../../asdg/05-high-level-design-and-architecture/docs/architectural-decisions.md) require the method for material architectural decisions in assigned documentation.
+The role's contract, native adapter, root instruction bridge and shared policies now agree on bounded decision-document authoring.
+The [package format](../../../asdg/skills/asdg-decision/record-format.md) specifies a named folder, one or two introductions, meaningful option notes, editable visuals and evidence.

+Canonical sources and thin discovery templates were added; the client adapter is installed without reinitializing project state.

+The documentation allowance does not authorize implementation, deployment, or formal document acceptance.
